newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids static as oil jumps, gas plunges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids static as oil jumps, gas plunges.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices were static Monday as the domestic crude oil and natural gas markets took opposite direction following the four-day Thanksgiving holiday weekend,
"It's been very quiet on the resid side," said a Gulf Coast physical dealer, despite swings in those other markets.
NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 25.1 cents at $3.246 per million British thermal units on technical maneuvering and lower cash prices in the U.S. Gulf.
NYMEX January crude oil futures finished up $1.05 at $24.80 a barrel, pushed higher on a gasoline-led rally.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent sulfur grade was still at $22.25-50 a barrel, with NYH December paper holding in the $22.15-$22.35 range.
NYH January one percent paper remained at $22.25-$22.50, with deals at $22.25 and $22.30 heard changing hands.
High sulphurs in NYH also were unchanged, with 2.2 percent continuing to be discussed on either side of $20.50.
In U.S. Gulf, one percent resid camped near $19.50 and three percent at $18.25-50. USG December three percent paper was discussed lower at $17.75-$18.00, down from Friday's notational $18.30-45.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York City gate swing gas fell to the low $4.00 area, down from Friday's $4.30s range compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent.
In December, New York gas was still assessed at about $4.75-90/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.53/mmBtu equivalent.
